keywords.def: investigate something in a new way in order to increase the range of your knowledge, understanding or experience
unable to see the difference between certain colours, especially green and red
without purpose or meaning, and a waste of time

keywords.term: I would say that, wouldn't I?
keywords.def: of course I would say that; used to imply there's some reason that what the speaker is saying is obviously biased towards them
based on personal opinions and feelings rather than on objective facts

sentences.en: Hello. This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎收听 BBC Learning English 的《6 Minute English》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Phil. And I'm Beth. Now, let's talk about food.
sentences.zh: 我是 Phil。我是 Beth。今天我们来聊聊食物。

sentences.en: OK. What food do you love? What food do you hate?
sentences.zh: 好的。你喜欢吃什么食物？讨厌吃什么食物？

sentences.en: If you ask around, you'll soon see there's no right or wrong answer – it's all a question of taste.
sentences.zh: 如果你去问问别人，很快就会发现这个问题没有标准答案——这完全是个人口味的问题。

sentences.en: But our taste, it turns out, isn't simply a matter of opinion.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，我们的口味并不仅仅是个人观点的问题。

sentences.en: Rather, scientists have discovered that taste is influenced by our genes and DNA.
sentences.zh: 科学家发现，味觉其实受到基因和 DNA 的影响。

sentences.en: So, in this programme we'll be asking, what is taste?
sentences.zh: 所以在这期节目中，我们要探讨的问题是：什么是味觉？

sentences.en: Why can't we agree on it? And is it worth listening to experts whose job is to tell us what to eat and drink?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们在口味上总是意见不一？听那些专门告诉我们该吃什么、喝什么的专家的话，真的有意义吗？

sentences.en: And, as usual, we'll be learning some useful new vocabulary as well.
sentences.zh: 像往常一样，我们也会学习一些实用的新词汇。

sentences.en: Great, but first I have a question for you, Beth.
sentences.zh: 太好了，不过在这之前，我有个问题要考考你，Beth。

sentences.en: A good way of finding out about British tastes is with the nation's best-loved snack, crisps.
sentences.zh: 了解英国人口味的一个好方法，就是看看这个国家最受欢迎的零食——薯片。

sentences.en: So, what is the most popular flavour of crisps in the UK?
sentences.zh: 那么，英国最受欢迎的薯片口味是什么呢？

sentences.en: Is it: a) salt and vinegar? b) cheese and onion? or, c) prawn cocktail?
sentences.zh: 是 a) 盐醋味？b) 奶酪洋葱味？还是 c) 鸡尾酒虾味？

sentences.en: I'm going to guess cheese and onion. OK, Beth, I'll reveal the answer later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 我猜是奶酪洋葱味。好的，Beth，答案我会在节目后面公布。

sentences.en: Science's understanding of how taste works started only 25 years ago with the discovery of taste receptors, cells located in the taste buds on your tongue.
sentences.zh: 科学界对味觉运作机制的认识，直到 25 年前发现味觉受体才真正开始——这是一种位于舌头味蕾中的细胞。

sentences.en: But people's taste is unique to them. What tastes sweet to me, might taste sour or salty to someone else, and this is because of differences in the receptors we're born with.
sentences.zh: 但每个人的味觉都是独一无二的。我觉得甜的东西，在别人尝来可能是酸的或咸的，这是因为我们天生的味觉受体存在差异。

sentences.en: In other words, taste is partly genetic.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，味觉在一定程度上是由基因决定的。

sentences.en: Here's Danielle Reed, researcher at the Monell Chemical Senses Center in Philadelphia explaining more to BBC World Service programme, 'The Food Chain': …when we first started doing genetic studies, we really just confined ourselves to looking at a few Europeans, people of European ancestry.
sentences.zh: 下面是费城莫奈尔化学感官中心研究员 Danielle Reed 在 BBC 世界服务频道节目《The Food Chain》中的进一步解释：……我们刚开始做基因研究的时候，其实只局限于研究少数欧洲人，也就是欧洲血统的人群。

sentences.en: And so, our understanding of the broad diversity of humans on the planet was extremely limited.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们对地球上人类广泛多样性的了解其实非常有限。

sentences.en: We are broadening our horizons and studying people of Asian and African ancestry, and that has really opened up the knowledge that people are much more diverse than we ever realised…
sentences.zh: 现在我们正在拓宽视野，研究亚洲和非洲血统的人群，这让我们真正认识到，人类的多样性远比我们以往所了解的要丰富得多……

sentences.en: And what you're saying is, "No, taste isn't a matter of opinion, it's a matter of biology".
sentences.zh: 你的意思是，'不，味觉不是主观看法的问题，而是生物学的问题'。

sentences.en: Exactly and we wouldn't... you know, for our friends who are colour-blind, we wouldn't chastise them for not being able to see red or for dressing in colours we don't appreciate, but we feel very free to criticise our friends' sense of taste.
sentences.zh: 没错，我们不会……你知道，对于色盲的朋友，我们不会因为他们分不清红色，或者穿了我们不喜欢的颜色而责怪他们，但我们却毫不犹豫地去批评朋友的口味。

sentences.en: It was only when scientists looked outside Europe to the rest of the world that they realised the diversity of human taste.
sentences.zh: 直到科学家把目光投向欧洲以外的世界，他们才意识到人类味觉的多样性。

sentences.en: Danielle says they broadened their horizons, they investigated something in a new way to increase their knowledge and understanding of it.
sentences.zh: Danielle 说他们拓宽了视野(broadened their horizons)，也就是用一种新方式去研究某件事，从而增进对它的了解和认识。

sentences.en: Danielle compares taste to another genetically controlled condition, being colour-blind or unable to see the difference between certain colours like green and red.
sentences.zh: Danielle 把味觉比作另一种由基因决定的状况——色盲，也就是无法分辨某些颜色，比如绿色和红色。

sentences.en: You wouldn't chastise – criticise or punish - someone for being colour-blind, so why criticise someone's taste?
sentences.zh: 你不会因为一个人色盲就去指责(chastise)——也就是批评或惩罚他，那为什么要批评别人的口味呢？

sentences.en: But, if scientists are telling us taste is largely genetic, what about restaurant critics and wine connoisseurs, people whose job it is to tell us what to eat and drink?
sentences.zh: 但如果科学家告诉我们味觉在很大程度上是基因决定的，那餐厅评论家和品酒行家又该怎么说呢？他们的工作就是告诉我们该吃什么、喝什么。

sentences.en: Are their opinions any better than our own?
sentences.zh: 他们的看法真的比我们自己的更高明吗？

sentences.en: Here's David Kermode, wine judge for the International Wine and Spirits Competition, speaking with Ruth Alexander for BBC World Service's, 'The Food Chain': Scientists have established that taste is individual and to a large extent actually genetic.
sentences.zh: 下面是国际葡萄酒与烈酒大赛评委 David Kermode 在 BBC 世界服务频道《The Food Chain》节目中与 Ruth Alexander 的对话：科学家已经证实，味觉因人而异，而且在很大程度上确实是由基因决定的。

sentences.en: So I wonder, does that render the wine competition a pointless exercise?
sentences.zh: 那我想问，这是不是意味着葡萄酒大赛其实毫无意义？

sentences.en: No. I mean, I would say that wouldn't I?
sentences.zh: 不，我是说，我当然会这么说，不是吗？

sentences.en: But of course, individual taste is subjective.
sentences.zh: 但当然，个人口味是主观的。

sentences.en: We all have our own personal prejudices in whatever sphere of life you want to go into, but we are encouraged, I mean ordered almost, to park those prejudices.
sentences.zh: 在生活的方方面面，我们都难免带有个人偏见，但我们被鼓励——甚至可以说是被要求——把这些偏见放到一边。

sentences.en: Since people's tastes are naturally different, Ruth asks if wine competitions are pointless, without purpose and a waste of time.
sentences.zh: 既然人们的口味天生就各不相同，Ruth 便问道，葡萄酒大赛是不是毫无意义(pointless)——也就是没有目的、纯属浪费时间。

sentences.en: Being a wine judge, David, of course disagrees, using the phrase, but I would say that, wouldn't I?
sentences.zh: 作为一名葡萄酒评委，David 当然不同意这种说法，他用了一句话：'我当然会这么说，不是吗？'

sentences.en: This phrase means something like, 'of course I would say that'.
sentences.zh: 这句话的意思大致是'我当然会这么说'。

sentences.en: It implies there's some reason that what the speaker is saying is obviously biased towards them.
sentences.zh: 它暗示说话人这么说显然是出于某种对自己有利的原因，带有偏向性。

sentences.en: David admits that taste is subjective, based on personal opinions and feelings rather than on facts.
sentences.zh: David 承认，口味是主观的(subjective)，基于个人的观点和感受，而非事实。

sentences.en: I think it's time to reveal the answer to your question, Phil.
sentences.zh: 我想是时候公布你那个问题的答案了，Phil。

sentences.en: Right. I asked for Britain's most popular flavour of crisp, and you said, cheese and onion which was… the correct answer!
sentences.zh: 好的。我问的是英国最受欢迎的薯片口味，你说是奶酪洋葱味，这……是正确答案！

sentences.en: OK, let's recap the vocabulary we've learned in this programme starting with the phrase to broaden or expand your horizons meaning 'to explore something in a new way which increases your knowledge and understanding of it'.
sentences.zh: 好，我们来回顾一下这期节目学到的词汇，先从短语 broaden/expand your horizons(拓宽视野)开始，意思是'以一种新方式去探索某事，从而增进对它的了解和认识'。

sentences.en: To chastise means to strongly punish or criticise.
sentences.zh: chastise 意思是严厉地惩罚或批评。

sentences.en: A colour-blind person is unable to distinguish certain colours especially greens and reds.
sentences.zh: 色盲(colour-blind)的人无法分辨某些颜色，尤其是绿色和红色。

sentences.en: Something which is pointless, has no purpose or meaning and is a waste of time.
sentences.zh: pointless(毫无意义)指的是没有目的、没有意义、纯属浪费时间的事情。

sentences.en: The phrase I would say that wouldn't I? is a tag question meaning, 'of course I would say that'.
sentences.zh: 短语 I would say that, wouldn't I？是一个反义疑问句，意思是'我当然会这么说'。

sentences.en: And finally, if something is subjective, it's influenced by personal beliefs or feelings, rather than based on facts.
sentences.zh: 最后，如果某事是主观的(subjective)，那就是受个人信念或感受影响，而非基于事实。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up. Goodbye for now!
sentences.zh: 六分钟又到了，我们先说再见！

sentences.en: Bye!
sentences.zh: 拜拜！
